phases.phase: 1. Enhanced Web App Manifest & App Icons
phases.description: Upgrade the existing site.webmanifest with complete metadata, generate raster PNG icons at standard sizes, and wire them into the root layout.
files_to_create_or_modify: src/app/layout.tsx (modify — add manifest link, theme-color meta, apple-touch-icon link)
implementation_steps: Step 1: Create scripts/generate-icons.mjs — a Node.js script that uses sharp to convert public/favicon.svg to PNG icons at 192x192, 256x256, 384x384, 512x512 in public/icons/, plus apple-touch-icon at 152x152 and 180x180 in public/icons/. Use sharp's SVG rendering with a fixed background color (#000000) for proper rasterization. This avoids manual icon generation.
Step 2: Add npm script "generate-icons": "node scripts/generate-icons.mjs" to package.json. Run it once to produce the icon files.

Step 3: Update public/site.webmanifest — add icons array with all raster sizes, add categories: ["portfolio", "technology", "development"], add scope: "/", add prefer_related_applications: false, add screenshots entry pointing to og-image.svg with a label. Keep existing SVG entries for backward compatibility.
Step 4: Add IS_PWA_ENABLED feature flag to src/lib/features.ts — export const IS_PWA_ENABLED = true;

Step 5: Modify src/app/layout.tsx — in the generateMetadata() function, add manifest: '/site.webmanifest' to the returned Metadata object. Add themeColor: '#000000'. Also add appleWebApp: { capable: true, statusBarStyle: 'black-translucent', title: 'JN Portfolio' }. Update the icons block to reference the new apple-touch-icon.png.
Step 6: Add <link rel="apple-touch-icon" sizes="180x180" href="/icons/apple-touch-icon-180x180.png" /> to the <head> sections in all three layout code paths (test, streaming, runtime).
Step 7: Run npm run build to verify no compilation errors and the manifest is accessible at /site.webmanifest.

phases.description: Rewrite public/sw.js with robust strategies: Cache-First for static assets, Stale-While-Revalidate for navigation, Network-First for dynamic API routes, and a proper offline fallback page. Integrate build-time cache manifest generation.
implementation_steps: Step 1: Create src/app/offline/page.tsx — a lightweight offline fallback page with the portfolio logo, a 'You are offline' message, and a 'Try again' button that calls window.location.reload(). Use Tailwind for styling to match the portfolio theme. Keep it under 10KB total.

Step 2: Create scripts/generate-sw-manifest.mjs — a Node.js script run after next build that reads the .next build manifest to extract all static asset URLs (_next/static/**/*.js, *.css, *.svg, etc.) and writes them to public/sw-assets.json as a JSON array of URL strings the SW can pre-cache. This ensures the SW always has an up-to-date asset list.

Step 3: Rewrite public/sw.js with the following architecture: (a) Import sw-assets.json at install time for pre-caching. (b) Use cache-first for /_next/static/*, /fonts/*, /icons/*, /favicon.svg, /apple-touch-icon.png with a dedicated STATIC_ASSETS cache. (c) Use stale-while-revalidate for navigation requests (mode === 'navigate') — serve from cache immediately, fetch update in background. (d) Use network-first for /api/* routes, /blog/*, /projects/* with dedicated API and PAGE caches. (e) On network failure for navigation, serve /offline page from cache. (f) Keep skipWaiting() and clients.claim() for immediate activation. (g) Add message event listener for manual cache invalidation.

Step 4: Add npm script "generate-sw-manifest": "node scripts/generate-sw-manifest.mjs" to package.json. Wire it into the build pipeline by appending && npm run generate-sw-manifest to the next build command in the build script.
Step 5: Update the CSP in next.config.js — ensure worker-src 'self' blob: already covers the SW registration. No change needed if already present (confirmed: line 33 has it).
Step 6: Run npm run build to verify the SW manifest is generated at public/sw-assets.json and the SW compiles/runs without errors.

phases.phase: 3. Offline UI Indicators & Service Worker Registration
phases.description: Build a useNetworkStatus hook for reactive online/offline state, an OfflineBanner component, and a ServiceWorker registration module.
implementation_steps: Step 1: Create src/hooks/useNetworkStatus.ts — a custom hook that initializes from navigator.onLine, listens to window 'online'/'offline' events, and returns { isOnline: boolean, wasOffline: boolean }. The wasOffline flag (stored in a ref) allows showing a one-time 'Back online' message after reconnection. Clean up event listeners on unmount.

Step 2: Create src/components/ui/OfflineBanner.tsx — a fixed bottom banner component that: (a) Renders null when online with no recent transition. (b) When offline, shows a non-intrusive amber/yellow banner with a Wi-Fi-off icon and text: 'You are currently offline. Browsing cached portfolio data.' (c) When transitioning back online after being offline, briefly shows a green 'Back online' banner for 3 seconds then fades out using CSS animation. (d) Respects prefers-reduced-motion. (e) Uses fixed positioning with bottom-0, proper z-index, and role="alert" for accessibility.

Step 3: Create src/lib/sw-register.ts — a utility module that registers the service worker from /sw.js with proper scope. Handles: (a) Registration only in production (skip in dev/test). (b) Update detection via 'updatefound' event. (c) Automatic skipWaiting on controller change. (d) Exports a registerSW() async function and a sendMessageToSW(type, data) function for cache invalidation from the app.

Step 4: Create src/components/ui/ServiceWorkerManager.tsx — a client component ("use client") that calls registerSW() on mount. Renders nothing (null). Gated behind IS_PWA_ENABLED flag. This keeps SW registration logic separate from the layout.
Step 5: Add IS_OFFLINE_BANNER_VISIBLE = true to src/lib/features.ts. This allows toggling the banner independently from the full PWA feature flag.

Step 6: Modify src/app/layout.tsx — import and render <OfflineBanner /> inside the <body> in all three code paths (before closing </body>). Import and render <ServiceWorkerManager /> inside the body only in the streaming and runtime paths (not in test path, since jsdom doesn't support SW registration).

Step 7: Run npm run test -- --run to verify existing tests still pass. Write a new test file at src/__tests__/hooks/useNetworkStatus.test.ts that verifies the hook returns correct values and responds to synthetic online/offline events.

phases.description: Integrate PWA asset generation into the build pipeline, ensure compatibility with both Vercel and Cloudflare Workers deployment targets, and add performance monitoring hooks.
files_to_create_or_modify: package.json (modify — wire generate-icons and generate-sw-manifest into build pipeline)
next.config.js (modify — add PWA-related headers for service worker and manifest)
public/_headers (modify — add SW and manifest caching rules for Cloudflare)
src/lib/features.ts (modify — finalize all PWA feature flags)
portfolio-v1/.gitignore (modify — add public/sw-assets.json and public/icons/ to track? No — keep generated files tracked so SW can access them. Remove if previously ignored.)
implementation_steps: Step 1: Update package.json build script — change from concurrently running next build and sanity build to: concurrently "next build && node scripts/generate-sw-manifest.mjs" "npm run build:studio". This ensures the SW manifest is generated after every production build. The generate-icons script is a one-time manual step (not run on every build).

Step 2: Update next.config.js — add a custom header for /sw.js with Cache-Control: no-cache, must-revalidate (so the SW is never cached by the browser's HTTP cache, ensuring updates are detected). Also add /icons/* with Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable.

Step 3: Update public/_headers for Cloudflare Workers deployment — add rules for /sw.js (Cache-Control: no-cache, must-revalidate) and /icons/* (Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable). This is critical for Cloudflare deployments where _headers overrides all other config.

Step 4: Ensure .gitignore does not exclude public/sw-assets.json or public/icons/*. Remove any ignore patterns that would exclude them. These files must be committed since they are served as static assets.

Step 5: Add a section to the existing testing protocol for PWA verification. Create a test file at src/__tests__/lib/sw-register.test.ts that tests the sendMessageToSW function (mocking ServiceWorker). Create src/__tests__/components/OfflineBanner.test.tsx for the OfflineBanner component.

Step 6: Run npm run build to verify end-to-end pipeline: next build succeeds, generate-sw-manifest.mjs runs and produces public/sw-assets.json, all routes still work. Run npm run test -- --run to verify all tests pass.
Step 7: Deploy to Vercel (or Cloudflare) and run Lighthouse PWA audit to verify the PWA checklist. Expected: Installable, configured, registers SW, offline fallback works.

code_snippets.public/_headers additions:
# SW must never be cached
/sw.js
  Cache-Control: no-cache, must-revalidate
  Service-Worker-Allowed: /

# Icons are immutable
/icons/*
  Cache-Control: public,max-age=31536000,immutable

# Manifest revalidates daily
/site.webmanifest
  Cache-Control: public,max-age=86400
code_snippets.package.json build script: "build": "concurrently --names next,sanity --prefix-colors cyan,magenta --kill-others-on-fail \"next build && node scripts/generate-sw-manifest.mjs\" \"npm run build:studio\""

testing_protocol: 1. Build verification: Run npm run build — verify next build succeeds and scripts/generate-sw-manifest.mjs runs, producing public/sw-assets.json with the correct asset list.
2. Unit tests: Run npm run test -- --run — ensure src/__tests__/hooks/useNetworkStatus.test.ts and src/__tests__/components/OfflineBanner.test.tsx pass.
3. Manifest validation: Open browser DevTools → Application → Manifest — verify all fields display correctly (name, icons, start_url, display, theme_color).
4. Service Worker registration: Open browser DevTools → Application → Service Workers — verify SW is registered from /sw.js with scope /.

5. Offline simulation (Chrome DevTools): Go to DevTools → Network tab → check 'Offline' checkbox. Navigate to any previously visited page — it should load from cache. Navigate to a page that hasn't been cached — it should show the /offline page gracefully.

6. Offline simulation (Lighthouse): Run Lighthouse audit → PWA category — verify 'Current page responds with 200 when offline', 'start_url responds with 200 when offline', and 'Is fast and reliable' pass.
7. Installability: In Chrome, verify the 'Install' icon appears in the address bar. On Android (Chrome), verify the Add to Home Screen prompt works.
8. Cache invalidation: After a new build/deploy, verify the SW updates correctly. The old cache should be deleted by the activate handler, and new assets pre-cached.
9. Cloudflare Workers compatibility: Deploy via npm run cloudflare:deploy. Verify the _headers file is respected, SW registers on the deployed URL, and offline fallback works on the edge.
10. Cross-browser: Verify on Firefox (about:debugging → Service Workers) and Safari (Developer → Service Workers) that registration and offline fallback work.
rollback_plan: If any PWA feature causes production issues: (1) Set IS_PWA_ENABLED = false and IS_OFFLINE_BANNER_VISIBLE = false in src/lib/features.ts and redeploy. This disables SW registration and offline banner without removing any code. (2) If the SW itself is problematic, the old public/sw.js (v4) is preserved in git history and can be restored via git checkout HEAD~1 -- public/sw.js. (3) The manifest and icons can be reverted by restoring public/site.webmanifest from git. (4) The /offline page is inert unless the SW explicitly routes to it — no action needed if SW is disabled.
story_breakdown: S-PWA-1: Generate raster PNG icons from SVG and update site.webmanifest with complete metadata
S-PWA-2: Wire manifest and apple touch icons into root layout with PWA-friendly metadata
S-PWA-3: Rewrite service worker with Cache-First, Stale-While-Revalidate, Network-First strategies
S-PWA-4: Create /offline fallback page with branded UI and retry button
S-PWA-5: Create useNetworkStatus hook with online/offline detection and wasOffline flag
S-PWA-6: Create OfflineBanner component with offline and reconnection messaging
S-PWA-7: Create SW registration module and ServiceWorkerManager component with message passing
S-PWA-8: Integrate SW manifest generation into build pipeline and configure headers for both Vercel and Cloudflare
S-PWA-9: Write tests for useNetworkStatus hook, OfflineBanner, and SW registration; run Lighthouse audit
